current_text.html: Whenever a minister of the Gospel shall habitually fail to be engaged in the regular discharge of his official functions, it shall be the duty of the Presbytery, at a stated meeting, to inquire into the cause of such dereliction and, if necessary, to institute judicial proceedings against him for breach of his covenant engagement. If it shall appear that his neglect proceeds only from his lack of acceptance to the Church, Presbytery may, upon the same principle upon which it withdraws license from a licentiate for lack of evidence of the divine call, divest him of his office without censure, even against his will, a majority of two-thirds (2/3) being necessary for this purpose. In such a case, the clerk shall under the order of the Presbytery forthwith deliver to the minister concerned a written note that, at the next stated meeting, the question of his being so dealt with is to be considered. This notice shall distinctly state the grounds for this proceeding. The party thus notified shall be heard in his own defense; and if the decision pass against him he may appeal, as if he had been tried after the usual forms. This principle may apply, with any necessary changes, to ruling elders and deacons.

relationships.title: Re-examination and divestiture of officers in rotational systems

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that the BCO provides no procedure for re-examining rotated-off officers' qualifications, but divestiture may only occur under BCO 24-6, 38-2, or 34-10.

relationships.title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation

occurrences.excerpt: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.

relationships.title: Effect of appeal on suspension of disciplinary censure during review

metadata.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained TE Craig Sheppard's complaint against Highlands Presbytery. It held that Presbytery erred when its Judicial Commission found a strong presumption of guilt but, instead of instituting process under BCO 31-2, directed pastoral reconciliation and conditioned later process on its success; that motion also impaired the accused's right against self-incrimination. It further held that BCO 32-20's one-year time bar had run and that the 2022 amendment did not apply retroactively, so Presbytery is debarred from prosecuting the allegations. Four commissioners dissented, disputing the BCO 32-20 ruling.

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed Great Lakes Presbytery’s divestiture of his office without censure under BCO 34-10. The SJC sustained his claim that Presbytery failed to make required findings that he habitually neglected official functions and that any neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church. It reversed and annulled the divestiture, leaving him a member in good standing, and required no further action. The other four specifications were moot. Presbytery remained free to pursue proper Chapter 31 process or a procedurally compliant BCO 34-10 divestiture.

metadata.synopsis: A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. Three specifications failed, while one duplicated another.

metadata.synopsis: Keating challenged Warrior Presbytery’s decision to divest him of ordination without censure while he was absent. The SJC sustained his appeal, reversed and voided the divestiture, and remanded because BCO 34-10’s required opportunity to be heard in his defense was not provided; this also amounted to hurrying before all testimony was taken. It rejected the reasonable-indulgence claim because Presbytery did not know of his postponement request. Keating remained a minister in good standing, but Presbytery could reconsider divestiture after reasonably soliciting a defense.

relationships.title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Sherfey challenged James River Presbytery’s denial of his complaint and alleged errors in its commission’s proceedings. The SJC ruled the complaint judicially out of order with incurable defects: several grounds had not first been adjudicated by Presbytery as BCO 43-2 required, and the General Assembly filing missed BCO 43-3’s thirty-day deadline. Incorrect advice from Presbytery’s clerk did not excuse compliance. The adopted decision neither reached the merits nor ordered a remand; only a concurrence proposed returning the matter to Presbytery.

metadata.synopsis: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority.

metadata.synopsis: A minister appealed three convictions and suspension that would automatically become indefinite absent repentance. The SJC sustained the appeal: unauthorized committee citations and admonition without process could not support guilt, and multiple trial violations were fatally prejudicial. It set aside the judgment, dismissed the citation and admonition charges, and revoked both censures. The inappropriate-language charge was not adjudicated on its merits; Presbytery could retry it on remand or dismiss it.

metadata.synopsis: After a minister remained on his presbytery's rolls without call and outside its bounds for more than seven years, the presbytery completed involuntary divestiture without censure. He appealed. The SJC denied the appeal and sustained the divestiture, reasoning that BCO 13-2 and 34-10 allowed the presbytery to follow that procedure once the constitutional three-year limit had long passed and no call to a particular ministry was available. The action therefore left the divestiture without censure in force.
